sections.content: You know the consequence markers *por lo tanto*, *por consiguiente* and *en consecuencia* from B2 Unit 31, and the purpose phrases *con el fin de*, *con miras a* and *con vistas a* from B2 Unit 12. An explanation chains them: a cause, what follows from it, and what a step is for. *Por consiguiente* states a real result, so the indicative follows it (*La levadura libera gas; por consiguiente, la masa aumenta.*). *De ahí que*, from the list of B2 Unit 31, also states a result, but the verb after it normally goes in the subjunctive (*La masa retiene el gas; de ahí que suba.*). *Con el fin de* + an infinitive says what a step is for.

sections.title: Result and purpose
rows: in order to (the purpose of a step)
con vistas a + infinitive or noun

items.spanish: La levadura libera gas; por consiguiente, la masa aumenta de volumen.
items.english: The yeast releases gas; consequently, the dough grows in volume.

items.spanish: La masa retiene el gas; de ahí que suba en el horno.
items.english: The dough holds the gas; hence it rises in the oven.

items.spanish: Se calienta el agua con el fin de activar la levadura.
items.english: The water is heated in order to activate the yeast.

items.spanish: Se pesa la muestra con vistas a repetir el experimento.
items.english: The sample is weighed with a view to repeating the experiment.

sections.content: *Por consiguiente* and *con el fin de* can both be "so" in English, but they point in opposite directions: *por consiguiente* gives a result that has happened, *con el fin de* gives the aim of a step. After *de ahí que*, use the subjunctive: it is the normal choice in careful writing. And *con el fin de* + an infinitive keeps the same subject in both parts; for a different subject use *para que* + the subjunctive (B1 Unit 4).
